# fldigi

**Multi-mode digital modem for PSK31, RTTY, Olivia, MT63 and more**

- **Version recorded:** 4.2.13
- **Categories:** `keyboard-modes`, `nbems`
- **Upstream:** <https://sourceforge.net/projects/fldigi/>
- **Also provides:** `flarq`
- **Needs first:** `libhamlib4t64`

## What it does

Turns a sound card and a transceiver into a modem for around twenty digital modes, including PSK31, RTTY, Olivia, Contestia and MT63, with a waterfall display for tuning them.

## Why you would want it

It is the reference implementation for HF digital modes on Linux and the foundation of the NBEMS emergency-messaging stack alongside flmsg and flamp.

## Before it will work

Sound-card audio routed to and from the radio, and PTT via hamlib, flrig, CAT, or a serial line. `docs/guides/digital-modes.md` covers rig control and the first PSK31 and RTTY contacts; `docs/guides/audio-routing.md` covers the audio path and choosing between fldigi's PulseAudio and PortAudio options.

## Install and launch

- **Installed with the profile:** [`digital-modes`](../profiles/digital-modes.md).
- **Install:** `hammunition install fldigi --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Commands it leaves on your PATH: `fldigi`, `flarq`.
- **The install needs the network to:** the upstream files the plan lists, each checked against a pinned digest (or, for map and reference data, the publisher or a LAN mirror).

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- source (autotools) from https://downloads.sourceforge.net/project/fldigi/fldigi/fldigi-4.2.13.tar.gz
  - build dependencies: `libfltk1.3-dev`, `libpng-dev`, `portaudio19-dev`, `libsamplerate0-dev`, `libsndfile1-dev`, `libudev-dev`
  - AHRL also installs libportaudio-ocaml-dev here. That is an OCaml binding fldigi does not use; it is a copy-paste error that never surfaced because AHRL checks no exit status. Deliberately omitted — see D-016.

Binaries this produces:

- `src/fldigi`
- `src/flarq`

This displaces the distribution's own `fldigi` (**D-022**: coexist, disclose, never remove silently).

## Known problems

The repository package is purged before installing, because the source build installs to the same prefix. The build also produces flarq, which is why this manifest declares it under provides — without that, a parity check reports flarq as a false gap.

## Toolkit risk

- `wx3.2`: unknown, checked 2026-08-25 — Not fldigi itself, but AHRL resolves libwxgtk*-dev by apt-cache grep for several units; fldigi uses FLTK and is unaffected. Recorded to keep the register honest about what was checked.
